text:
maria: heads up — running the sample edge app from our monorepo (pnpm workspace) and hitting an ESM/CJS resolution + auth retry problem.
maria: error in the edge runtime: `Uncaught SyntaxError: The requested module '/node_modules/@redwood/sdk/dist/index.cjs' does not provide an export named 'default'`
dan: ouch. that looks like the bundler pulled the CJS entry instead of the ESM one. are you seeing multiple copies of @redwood/sdk in the node_modules tree?
maria: ran `pnpm why @redwood/sdk` — it's hoisted to the root, but each package has a symlink to the local package. sometimes the build resolves `index.cjs` instead of `index.mjs`.
kai: bundlers/edge runtimes (esbuild in Vercel/Cloudflare) use different resolution rules for `exports`. if `package.json` has both `import` and `require`, some older resolvers default to require.
sam: also noticed an auth issue — after a retry the request goes out w/o Authorization header and we get a bunch of 401s. retry loop spins but token never attached on subsequent attempts.
maria: yeah the auth state looks like it's set on a different instance of the auth client — I think the symlink/hoist created two instances so the singleton didn't carry over.
lina: can you paste the `exports` in package.json and your pnpm version?
maria: sure — snippet: 
```
{
  "name": "@redwood/sdk",
  "exports": {
    ".": {
      "import": "./dist/index.mjs",
      "require": "./dist/index.cjs"
    }
  },
  "types": "./dist/index.d.ts"
}
```
pnpm: 7.21.0
dan: ok. short-term: force the bundler to prefer ESM — alias `@redwood/sdk` -> `@redwood/sdk/dist/index.mjs` in your rollup/webpack/esbuild config. that should avoid picking the CJS file.
kai: another workaround is set tsconfig `moduleResolution` to `bundler` and ensure the build tool is aware of `exports`.
sam: for the auth singleton problem we patched an internal lib to attach the client to `globalThis.__redwood_sdk_singleton__` so symlinked copies share the same instance. it helped us before in similar mono setups.
maria: tried the global singleton hack — that fixed the 401/retry case. aliasing fixed the runtime import. but TypeScript still complains about duplicated types (`Duplicate identifier 'ClientOptions'`).
lina: for types, use a single types entry and ensure `paths` in the workspace tsconfig points to the hoisted copy, or set `skipLibCheck: true` as a stopgap. We should also publish a single flattened `index.d.ts` to avoid per-package duplicates.
dan: filing follow-ups: 1) docs: recommended pnpm workspace setup for edge sample app, 2) SDK: consider exporting a stable ESM entrypoint that's always picked by bundlers, 3) SDK: consider global singleton pattern for auth or provide an opt-in init hook.
ploy-bot: 

deploy-bot: opened issue #842: "workspace-resolution: edge/esm/auth-singleton" with repro requested — @maria please add minimal repro steps and your pnpm lockfile.
maria: added a tiny repro (monorepo + sample edge function) and steps in the issue. thanks everyone! :thumbsup:
dan: nice. capture notes in the devex docs so teams don't re-run into this.
lina: will add a short how-to for alias and tsconfig tips.
sam: also — logging idea: surface when SDK instance count > 1 in dev builds so people spot duplicate installs earlier.
maria: agreed. logging would have saved me a day. thanks all.
